article_title: Not another computer algebra system: Highlighting wxMaxima in calculus
citation: Karjanto, N.; Husain, H.S. (2021). Not Another Computer Algebra System: Highlighting wxMaxima in Calculus. Mathematics 2021, 9, 1317. https://doi.org/10.3390/math9121317
title: Hermite-reduction-based integration account of wxMaxima's symbolic-integration limitations
description: The article explains wxMaxima's weakness in rational-function integration algorithmically: wxMaxima "implements the combination of Hermite reduction with either the partial fraction decomposition (Bernoulli–Leibniz algorithm)" for the rational part of the integrand, or heuristic methods for easier transcendental cases. Commercial systems such as Axiom and the 3M software employ more contemporary and advanced methods for the remaining terms after Hermite reduction. This account explains the failure patterns shown in Examples 7–10.
requirements: The account applies to indefinite integrals of rational functions, where wxMaxima still uses the algorithms described by Moses
constraints: The authors note the field of symbolic integration, particularly across different CAS, is a wide range and their examples are not exhaustive
target_learning_goals: understanding symbolic integration of rational functions and the capabilities and limits of computer algebra systems
examples: Example 7 shows Gärtner's integral becoming tractable in wxMaxima after a change-of-variables substitution command
key_sources: Karjanto, N.; Husain, H.S. (2021). Not Another Computer Algebra System: Highlighting wxMaxima in Calculus. Mathematics 2021, 9, 1317. https://doi.org/10.3390/math9121317

title: wxMaxima: free document-based GUI for the Maxima computer algebra system
description: wxMaxima is "a document-based graphical user interface (GUI) for the CAS Maxima" that allows use of all of Maxima's functions and "provides convenient wizards for accessing the most commonly used features, including inline plots and simple animations". It is free under the GNU General Public License, runs natively on Windows, Mac OS X, Linux, FreeBSD, Solaris and Android, installs in under three minutes, and is updated approximately twice annually. The combined educational-license cost of the commercial 3M software is almost USD 5500, while Maxima is free.
requirements: An executable file downloaded from Maxima's website or SourceForge, and an Internet connection for installation
constraints: Diophantine equation solvers and quantifier elimination are absent in wxMaxima, and a formula editor is missing in Maxima itself
target_learners: users in less affluent countries with limited resources
target_learning_goals: sketching 2D and 3D functions and parametric surfaces
examples: Table 2 shows commands computing lim sin(7x)/x at 0, the derivative of cos(3x²), and definite and indefinite integrals of 1/(1+x²)
Table 3 and Table 4 show parametric plots of a cardioid, a helix, a Möbius band and a torus
